text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: GPU request queue for inference-gpu-pool exceeded 9.8k pending requests. Autoscaler not increasing capacity. HPA metrics adapter reporting 5xxs. Paging on-call. https://incidents/redwood/1769123456

Sasha: paging @oncall-infra — can you take? high customer impact, some Dedicated customers seeing >500ms token latency spikes.

oncall-infra: on it — investigating HPA path. first glance: prometheus-adapter returning 502/503 to the HPA.

Diego: I can join. hint: earlier today we merged a metrics exporter for per-tenant token-rate that exploded cardinality. could be related.

Priya: adding context — we saw a slow scrape on prometheus around 17:05 UTC and adapter latencies spiked. If adapter times out, HPA won't see the custom metric and scaling will stall.

Marta: checking k8s events for the gpu-pool HPA: `Events: LastSeen 1m (x100) FailedGetMetrics` -> `failed to get external metrics from resource: adapter error: 502`

Diego: running quick checks: `kubectl -n monitoring logs deployment/prometheus-adapter` shows repeated `error fetching timeseries: context deadline exceeded` and `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address` in one adapter pod.

deploy-bot: deploy marker: `prometheus-exporter v2.9.0` rolled at 2026-03-15T17:01:12Z by ci/cd.

Sasha: ok mitigation plan: (1) prevent further autoscale decisions depending on flaky adapter (2) manually scale GPU pool to absorb queue (3) reduce load by routing low-priority inference to fallback small instances (4) fix/replace adapter.

Priya: step 1: flip HPA to fallback metric using k8s resource metrics (gpu_utilization) — patching now: `kubectl patch hpa/gpu-pool -p '{"spec": {"metrics": [{"type":"Resource","resource":{"name":"nvidia.com/gpu_utilization","targetAverageValue":"60"}}]}}'`

Diego: applied patch. HPA now reads resource metric but it needs node-level telemetry. Meanwhile manual scale to buy time: `kubectl -n inference scale deployment/gpu-workers --replicas=14` — replicas increased from 6->14.

Marta: queue length still high but ingress throttling reduced after scale. Token processing throughput increased by ~2.3x per pod.

Sasha: step 2: restart metrics stack components to clear stuck state: `kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter` and `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/metrics-server` — Priya doing restart.

Priya: restarted adapter pods one-by-one to avoid making Prom scrapes worse. logs now show adapter healthy in one pod, other pods OOMing frequently. increasing adapter replica memory and restarting.

Diego: found root cause signal: new exporter added a high-cardinality label `tenant_request_id` to a counter which made prometheus scrape ~10M series for a single metric. Adapter timed out while aggregating. Patch queued to strip that label from export.

Sasha: customer impact summary (preliminary): 7 Dedicated customers experienced increased latencies and intermittent 429 throttles between 16:58-17:28 UTC. No data exfiltration. CS alerted customers with temporary mitigation steps (route to hosted fallback).

cs-lead: adding from CS — we notified top 10 affected accounts, provided mitigation links and suggested using hosted endpoint until full fix. Two customers opened support P1s complaining about timeout errors in retries.

oncall-infra: after adapter restart and manual scaling, HPA eventually resumed using the fallback resource metric. Autoscaling started to react slowly but queue is draining — from 9.8k -> 2.1k in 18 minutes.

Diego: pushed hotfix to exporter to drop tenant_request_id label and to add relabeling in scrape config: `relabel_configs: - source_labels: [__name__] regex: 'high_card_metric' action: replace replacement: '$1'` (we'll refine).

Priya: Prometheus compacted and adapter warmed caches; verified `kubectl -n monitoring get --raw '/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1'` returns expected metric payload. HPA back to external metric path and scaling trending back to target.

Sasha: mitigation complete timeline: start 16:58 UTC (alert), manual scale 17:06, adapter restarts & hotfix 17:18, HPA resumed 17:36, queue drained to acceptable levels 17:46. Marking incident as mitigated but not resolved.

Marta: action items to be tracked: - revert temporary HPA patch after verification - add circuit-breaker/timeout on adapter side - add cardinality alert and pre-agg rules - improve runbook for metrics adapter failure - test autoscale in staging with high-cardinality injection

cs-lead: CS follow-ups: prepare customer-facing incident note with timeline, impact, and mitigation. Offer credits per SLA for affected customers where appropriate.

Sasha: assigning postmortem lead: Priya. SRE follow-ups assigned to Diego (fix exporter) and Marta (runbook + alerts). Priya to own timeline + RCA draft.

Priya: quick notes for RCA: root cause = unbounded cardinality from new exporter label + insufficient adapter timeouts and lack of circuit-breaker. Contributing = no cardinality gating in CI, missing autoscale fallback runbook automation.

Diego: temporary precaution: applied quota on Prom scrape length for that exporter, and added an ingress rule to route low-priority requests to hosted fallback for 24h to avoid recurrence while we fix infra.

Sasha: final operational checklist before we close this thread: 1) confirm all HPA are back to external metric behavior 2) confirm adapter memory stable for 24h 3) post incident note drafted 4) customer outreach complete.

deploy-bot: CI: exporter hotfix build passed and deployed to monitoring-canary.

Marta: will run a post-deploy chaos test in staging to simulate high-cardinality metric and validate autoscaling fallback. ETA 48h.

Priya: postmortem ETA: first draft in 48 hours, will include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and follow-ups.

Sasha: thanks everyone — great coordination. tagging this P0 as "mitigated" and keeping page open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
